what_it_does: Phone and laptop batteries (typically 6–8.4V from two cells) can charge via USB or deliver power back to USB devices (USB Power Delivery). Traditional converter chips waste energy in their inductors—the coils that store energy temporarily. This design uses a 'half-inductor-current' topology that cuts peak inductor current in half, dramatically reducing resistive losses in the inductor. An adaptive control loop adjusts the operating point moment-to-moment, achieving 97.4% peak efficiency in both charging and power-delivery modes, enabling smaller, cooler converters.
